intuition: Save running totals once, before answering queries. Let prefix[i] be the sum of the first i values. A range sum is the total through its right end minus the total before its left end. This makes every later query a single subtraction.

prefix[k] stores the sum of the first k values, including prefix[0]=0 for the empty prefix. A query from left through right consists of the prefix through right with everything before left removed. Its answer is therefore prefix[right+1]-prefix[left]. The extra initial zero makes a query starting at index zero use the same expression as every other query.

This indexing convention separates element positions from prefix boundaries. The element at index right belongs in the query, so its enclosing prefix ends at boundary right+1. Negative values and zero do not require any special handling because subtraction cancels the unwanted prefix exactly.

Constructor work is linear and each query is constant time, trading one additional array for faster repeated access. An update operation would invalidate these stored prefixes, but updates are explicitly outside this class’s interface.

steps: Accumulating one value at a time produces prefix=[0,-2,-2,1,-4,-2,-3].
sumRange(0,2) subtracts prefix[0]=0 from prefix[3]=1, giving 1.
sumRange(2,5) subtracts prefix[2]=-2 from prefix[6]=-3, giving -1.
sumRange(0,5) reads the complete total -3. The three query results are [1,-1,-3].
